paragraphs: (Avital, David’s wife, II Samuel 3:4.) According to Hyman, the scribe reports in Rav’s name three times in Moed Katan 18a: twice in aggadah and once in halakhah. Hyman calls the reading “in the name of Rav Pappa” a scribal error.

notes.text: The parenthetical Biblical Avital is not identified with the scribe. II Samuel 3:4 names Avital as Shefatyah’s mother; the supplied source has the irregular book label שמואל כ׳. The consulted Moed Katan text gives Rav Papa in all three statements, whereas Hyman favors Rav and calls the Papa reading erroneous. His judgment is preserved as such. The abbreviated title on the scribe does not settle Rav versus Rabbi.

Hyman owns the Rav-versus-Rav-Papa scribal-error judgment, with three reports, two aggadic and one halakhic, preserved. Earlier MoedKatan18a comparisons remain inherited, not a new primary inspection. The biblical namesake and the scribe are not identified. Supplied שמואל כ׳ פ״ג-ד remains a source-label question beside contextual II Samuel3:4. No new full-title witness determines the abbreviated heading.

On Moed Katan 18a, Rabbinovicz’s Dikdukei Soferim lists Rav Pappa in its printed-text column and Rav in its manuscript column in all three reports by Avitul the scribe. This supplies a witness for the attribution Hyman prefers. His judgment that Rav Pappa is a scribal error remains his own.
